$comment: The conformance suites, declared once. `generate_ci.py` emits the oracle jobs of
.github/workflows/ci.yml from this file, and `run_suite.py` runs one suite locally with
exactly the same steps, so the two cannot drift.
Every suite states what is compared and, where anything is canonicalized away, why. That
`why` used to live in a YAML comment next to a copy of the comparator; it is the part that
must not be lost, because canonicalization is how a bit-identity claim quietly weakens.
`status` is either `oracle-backed` (the golden is regenerated by the oracle in CI and
compared, which is the bar) or `unchecked` (the golden is committed and read by the Rust
tests, but no CI step has ever regenerated it against the oracle). See
docs/decisions/0008 for what the unchecked goldens turned out to be.

ci.$why: Suites are grouped into jobs of this size. One job per suite would restore the ~1 GB oracle image once per suite, which costs more runner time than it buys; one job for everything is what the hand-written workflow did, and it hid every suite after the first failure.

suites.title: the metrics rows
suites.why: The BAM hex and the two header lines carry JVM-chosen temp paths and a timestamp, so only the metrics body is comparable across runs. That is stated rather than left implicit, because a comparison that quietly ignores most of a file is worthless.

rules.why: One list, applied to every file, because a multi-tool harness emits more than one command-line header and stripping only the current tool's leaves the others' temp paths in place. That bug made CI report 14 mismatches that were not divergences at all.

suites.title: CollectRnaSeqMetrics
suites.why: Only the metrics body is comparable: the command-line header carries JVM temp paths and the Started-on line a timestamp. The sam/refflat/ribosomal input rows are compared raw, since a fixed seed and fixed content make them reproducible; a drift there would change what the Rust test parses.

rules.why: Command line (temp paths) and start time.

suites.title: CollectQualityYieldMetricsSNVQ
suites.why: Only the metrics body is comparable; the sam row is deterministic (hand-built reads) and is what the Rust test parses, so it is compared raw.

rules.why: Command line (temp paths) and start time.

suites.title: SamToFastq
suites.why: FASTQ output has no header lines, and the bam row is deterministic hex, so both rows are compared raw.

suites.title: FastqToSam
suites.why: FastqToSam writes no @PG and no timestamp, so the whole SAM (and the FASTQ input) are compared raw.

suites.title: SortSam
suites.why: SortSam changes only the header SO field and writes no @PG or timestamp, so every SAM is compared raw.

suites.title: AddOrReplaceReadGroups
suites.why: Adds no @PG and no timestamp and does not re-sort, so the whole file is compared raw.

suites.title: CleanSam
suites.why: CleanSam adds no @PG and no timestamp, so the whole file is compared raw.

suites.title: FixMateInformation
suites.why: Adds no @PG and no timestamp, so the whole file is compared raw.

suites.title: AddOATag
suites.why: AddOATag adds no @PG and no timestamp and preserves the order, so the whole SAM is compared raw.

suites.title: DownsampleSam
suites.why: The @PG record carries the command line (temp paths), which differs between the machine that committed the golden and this runner, so it is stripped from both sides before comparison, exactly as the conformance test does.

rules.why: @PG CL: is the command line, which holds run-specific temp paths.

suites.title: FilterSamReads
suites.why: Keeps the input sort order and adds no @PG and no timestamp, so each SAM is compared raw.

suites.title: CreateSequenceDictionary
suites.why: The UR field is the reference's file: URI, which differs between the machine that committed the golden and this runner, so it is stripped from both sides; @HD and each SN/LN/M5 are compared raw.

rules.why: Path-dependent reference URI. Restricted to the dict row so the inputs beside it stay raw.

suites.title: SamFormatConverter
suites.why: The BAM is written with the JDK deflater in the harness (USE_JDK_DEFLATER=true), so its BGZF blocks come from zlib and are reproducible here; input and output rows are compared raw in both directions.

suites.title: ValidateSamFile
suites.why: The report rows are deterministic text, so every case is compared raw.

suites.title: CompareSAMs
suites.why: CmpCorpus.java already strips the banner on the Java side, so the committed rows carry no timestamp and are compared raw.

suites.title: SplitSamByNumberOfReads and SplitSamByLibrary
suites.why: The corpus has several `shard` (respectively `file:<base>`) rows per case, so the full line sequence is compared rather than a (kind, case) key, which would collapse the shards.

suites.title: MergeSamFiles
suites.why: Several `input` rows per case, so the full line sequence is compared.

suites.title: Rows the reference refuses
suites.why: The covering arrays are generated over combinations the tool accepts, so the rejections they used to spend rows on are no longer exercised anywhere (decision 0009). A port that processes what Picard refuses is not byte-identical, so the exit path and the message are recorded here. The fixture directory is a per-run temporary path and the harness replaces it with <FIXTURES>: the message is behaviour, the path is not. From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner, published as the candidate-goldens artefact of the main run 33015632980, and byte for byte what this laptop produced.
expect_contains: should be coordinate sorted but the header says the sort order is queryname
suites.$expect_why: A row count is not evidence. The first run of this suite mounted no fixtures and produced four rows of 'Cannot read non-existent file', which the count alone accepted. These three phrases are the behaviours the suite exists for.

cases.why: No golden yet, and none may be committed from here: the bit-identity contract accepts goldens produced on real x86-64 CI, and this harness has so far only run in an emulated container. The generated job runs it and uploads the dump; committing that artefact is what turns this suite oracle-backed. Decision 0008 is what a golden of unknown provenance costs.

suites.title: QualityScoreDistribution
suites.why: A metrics file like the others in tools/metrics-conformance, but its dump was never wired into CI: the golden has only ever been compared against itself by the Rust test.

rules.why: Command line (temp paths) and start time, the same two lines the Rust test canonicalizes.

suites.title: CollectGcBiasMetrics

rules.why: Command line (temp paths) and start time, the same two lines the Rust test canonicalizes.

suites.why: The `bam` line is the hex of the input BAM, and that BAM's header carries a @SQ UR: pointing at a per-run temporary FASTA, so its bytes cannot match across runs. Everything else is compared raw: the reference bases the harness generated from a seeded Random, the detail metrics and the summary metrics, minus the two lines Picard stamps with its own command line and start time.

suites.title: AccumulateQualityYieldMetrics
suites.why: The tool writes a bare MetricsFile with no command-line or start-time header comments, so the whole file is compared raw with no canonicalization.

suites.title: BedToIntervalList
suites.why: The harness writes its fixtures under Files.createTempDirectory, so the @SQ UR: field is a fresh path on every run and cannot be compared across machines. Everything else, the @SQ order and the intervals, is compared raw.

rules.why: Per-run temp path in the sequence dictionary the harness builds.

suites.title: IntervalListToBed
suites.why: Same per-run UR: path as BedToIntervalList; the BED output itself carries no path.

rules.why: Per-run temp path in the input interval list's header.

suites.title: IntervalListTools
suites.why: IntervalListTools writes an @PG whose CL is the command line (temp paths), which the Rust test already strips, and the interval lists carry the per-run UR: path.

rules.why: @PG CL: is the command line, with the run's temp paths.
Per-run temp path in the sequence dictionary the harness builds.

suites.title: IntervalListTools PADDING and BREAK_BANDS_AT_MULTIPLES_OF
suites.why: PADDING pads every input interval before the action, clamped to the contig, and BREAK_BANDS_AT_MULTIPLES_OF splits the final intervals at band multiples and renames them A.1, A.2, A.3. Both change the output bytes and neither was exercised by the three existing cases.

rules.why: @PG CL: is the command line, with the run's temp paths.
Per-run temp path in the sequence dictionary the harness builds.

suites.$expect_why: Two cases, four rows each: the input list, PADDING, BREAK_BANDS, and the output.

cases.why: Produced by the pinned container on real x86-64 in CI run 30572202009, not on a laptop, which is the provenance decision 0008 exists to enforce.

suites.title: LiftOverIntervalList

rules.why: Per-run temp path in the target dictionary, which the tool copies verbatim into its output.

suites.why: The harness writes its fixtures under a temporary directory, so the target dictionary's UR: field is a fresh path on every run and LiftOverIntervalList copies it verbatim into its output. That one field is stripped; the @SQ order, the lifted intervals and their names are compared raw.

suites.title: ExtractSequences
suites.why: The extracted FASTA carries no path; the interval-list input row does, through its @SQ header.

rules.why: Per-run temp path in the input interval list's header.

suites.title: ScatterIntervalsByNs

rules.why: Per-run temp path in the reference dictionary, copied into the output interval list.

suites.why: The harness writes its reference under a temporary directory, so the dictionary's UR: field is a fresh path on every run and ScatterIntervalsByNs copies it into every output interval list. That one field is stripped; the scatter boundaries, the ACGT and N interval types and the @SQ order are compared raw.

suites.title: NonNFastaSize
suites.why: The output is a count and a newline; nothing in it is machine-dependent.

suites.title: NormalizeFasta
suites.why: Plain text in, plain text out; compared raw.

suites.title: SamToFastqWithTags
suites.why: FASTQ has no header, so each file is compared raw; the input SAM row carries the per-run UR: path.

rules.why: Per-run temp path in the input SAM's @SQ header.

suites.title: MergeBamAlignment
suites.why: The record corpus has several data-line rows under one (kind, case) key, so the full line sequence is compared; a keyed comparison would silently keep only the last row of each case.

suites.title: MergeBamAlignment, whole file
suites.why: The whole output SAM, header included. The @SQ UR: is the harness's per-run temp path, so it is stripped; the @PG records are compared raw, because MergeBamAlignment's PG linkage is exactly what this suite exists to check.

rules.why: Per-run temp path in the reference dictionary the harness builds.

suites.title: the map from VCF path to sample name, and the order its lines come out in
suites.why: PENDING: written once the measurement is read.

cases.why: PENDING: written once the measurement is read.

probes.title: Decision 0020 (htsjdk-rs): is CollectRnaSeqMetrics order-independent?
probes.on_failure: CollectRnaSeqMetrics is no longer order-independent. htsjdk-rs decision 0020 must be revisited.
probes.why: OverlapDetector in htsjdk-rs skips a byte-exact IntervalTree because the overlap set is folded commutatively by this Picard tool. The probe belongs here, not in htsjdk-rs, because it instantiates CollectRnaSeqMetrics and only the Picard oracle has it. Two runs differ iff the HashSet<Gene> order reaches the output; identical means it does not.
